title: Chicken breast, grilled without sauce, skin eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken breast is a lean, boneless cut taken from the bird's chest. When grilled without sauce and with the skin left on, it retains its natural flavor and the modest amount of healthy fats found in the skin.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast is the leanest part of the bird, containing very little fat when the skin is removed.
Grilling quickly sears the meat, preserving most of its protein and B‑vitamin content.
Leaving the skin on adds about 10 % of the total calories but also provides beneficial monounsaturated fats and vitamin K2.
Poultry is one of the most affordable sources of high‑quality protein worldwide.
Grill cooking imparts a smoky aroma that is enhanced by using wood chips.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving of chicken breast delivers roughly 31 g of complete protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Chicken breast contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb and ketogenic diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in niacin (B3), vitamin B6 and B12, which support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Beneficial fats in the skin
items.content: The skin provides monounsaturated fats and small amounts of omega‑6 fatty acids that can help promote satiety.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Chicken supplies selenium, phosphorus and zinc, important for immune health and bone strength.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked poultry may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: A small number of people can develop allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the breast has been pre‑marinated, sodium levels can be high; choose an unsalted version when possible.

items.title: Fat in the skin
items.content: While the skin adds flavor and healthy fats, excess can increase the dish’s calorie density.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the grilled breast for main‑course servings, add it to salads, sandwiches or wraps. The skin can be left on for extra taste or removed for a leaner option. It pairs well with grilled vegetables, lemon juice, and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw chicken in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for no more than 2 days. Cool cooked breast to room temperature, then place in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 3 days. For longer keeping, freeze in a sealed bag for up to 6 months.
